solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dog attracted to chicken dish with prawn

indicators.note: the following piece is drawn onto the end of the one before

parts.note: a cock is a male chicken
to dog someone is to tail or follow them

explanation.surface: A dog is drawn to a chicken dish that has prawns in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A prawn cocktail is a classic starter, so the drink-named dish is one served with prawn.

clue.text: Trainees, central pairing from Tredegar, to join Lions?

indicators.note: the pair is set in among the letters of the other piece, joining it

parts.note: lions are big cats

indicators.note: the middle two letters of the eight-letter word Tredegar are taken

explanation.surface: Young recruits from the Welsh town of Tredegar are being paired up to join the Lions rugby side.
explanation.walkthrough: Tredegar is a town in Wales; the British and Irish Lions are a touring rugby team, so 'Lions' looks like the rugby side but is just big animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadets are young people under training, for the forces or police.

clue.text: Fleshy melon bum wobbling to Paul

parts.note: can is US slang for the buttocks

indicators.note: the words to Paul are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's ample backside wobbles as they move towards Paul.
explanation.definitionFit: The cantaloupe is a variety of melon with sweet orange flesh, here in its older spelling.

clue.text: He, devil, whose tail unseen, noticed my horribly hellish work

indicators.note: the letters are thrown into a horrible jumble
the last letter of devil is not to be seen, so it is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone spots a tailless devil in a horrid, hellish piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whose tail unseen' cuts DEVIL to DEVI; 'horribly' rearranges HE + DEVI + NOTICED + MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's epic poem opens with the Inferno, a journey through Hell, so it is a work about the underworld.

clue.text: Published at home design from plate

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a print is an image made from an engraved plate

explanation.surface: A design printed from an engraving plate is released at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A book that is in print is published and available to buy.

clue.text: Writer on slavery died in luggage compartment?

parts.note: Harriet Beecher Stowe wrote the anti-slavery novel Uncle Tom's Cabin
d is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: An anti-slavery author died inside a luggage compartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags put away in the hold have been stowed, packed away for the journey.

clue.text: She thought Eliot could create novel

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase could be remade into something new

explanation.surface: A woman reckoned T. S. Eliot might write a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could create' rearranges SHE THOUGHT ELIOT. The novel is by Virginia Woolf, the answer at 17/7.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the 1927 novel by Woolf about the Ramsay family and a trip across the bay.

clue.text: See 17
Called into action — driven mad

indicators.note: the first piece is put inside the second

parts.note: a deed is an action
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: Someone was summoned into action, having been driven to madness.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deranged has been made insane, unhinged.

clue.text: Caught wearing make up right now

indicators.note: the second piece wears the first like a garment around it

parts.note: to atone is to make up for a wrong
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is caught with make-up on and told to remove it immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at once means doing it immediately.

clue.text: Rage in The Iliad excited fiery poet

indicators.note: the phrase's letters are stirred up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The anger in Homer's epic stirs up a passionate poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges RAGE IN THE ILIAD. The Iliad does open on Achilles' rage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian poet of the Inferno is fiery in the sense that he wrote of Hell's flames.

clue.text: Winger after training with team gets cake or biscuit

indicators.note: the bird comes after the training in the answer

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise training
a winger is a bird, and a tit is a small bird
a four is a rowing crew of four

explanation.surface: A rugby winger, after training with the squad, is given a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Petits fours are small fancy cakes or biscuits served with coffee.

clue.text: Routine deportation former spouse avoids

indicators.note: the former spouse is kept out, removed from the longer word

parts.note: extradition is the sending of someone to another country for trial
an ex is a former husband or wife

explanation.surface: A former spouse dodges a routine deportation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is an established custom, a routine handed down.

clue.text: Whirling river drowns female, small and delicate

indicators.note: the river closes over the female, holding her inside
the river's name spins round to read backwards

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river

explanation.surface: A woman is drowned in a river's whirlpool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whirling' turns NILE to ELIN, which takes F inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes a slight, dainty, pixie-like build.

clue.text: Council drunk has internal struggle

indicators.note: the struggle is placed inside the drunk

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
to vie is to compete, struggle

explanation.surface: A drunken council is torn by internal power struggles.
explanation.definitionFit: A soviet was an elected workers' council in revolutionary Russia.

clue.text: Example chapter taken from long story book

indicators.note: the chapter is removed from the long story

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: An example chapter is extracted from a long story in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect example, the embodiment of a type.

clue.text: Strange man finds fraternal member

parts.note: odd means strange
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A peculiar man turns up as a member of a brotherhood.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oddfellows are a friendly society, a fraternal order with members across Britain and America.

clue.text: American state seducer straddles old writer

parts.note: Virginia is a US state

indicators.note: the seducer sits astride the old, enclosing it

parts.note: a wolf is a predatory seducer

explanation.surface: A seducer from the American South takes up with an old author.
explanation.definitionFit: The modernist novelist of the Bloomsbury group, author of Mrs Dalloway, was a writer.

clue.text: Grab Victoria for example — leader I must replace

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is the one changed
the letter I goes in where the first letter was

parts.note: Queen Victoria was also Empress of India

explanation.surface: A woman is told to grab Queen Victoria, and that she must replace the leader.
explanation.walkthrough: To impress is to seize men for service, as press gangs did.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress is to seize or commandeer, especially to force into military service.

clue.text: Song social worker gets embarrassed about

indicators.note: the embarrassed piece goes round the worker

parts.note: shy means bashful, embarrassed
an ant is a worker insect living in colonies

explanation.surface: A social worker grows embarrassed about singing a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a sailors' work song.

clue.text: Compound that dresses horse leather

indicators.note: the compound clothes the horse, wrapped around it

parts.note: an oxide is a chemical compound of oxygen
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A chemical compound is used to dress horse leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxhide is the skin of an ox, tanned as leather.

clue.text: Developed moronic character

indicators.note: the word's letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A stupid character has evolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developed' rearranges MORONIC; the surface nods to the Covid variant named after this letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, a written character.

clue.text: Offensive as the rich can be!

definitions.meaning: the very wealthy are said to be stinking or extremely rich

explanation.definitionFit: Filthy means foul or obscene, and in the idiom filthy rich it means extremely wealthy.

clue.text: Reptile to travel round financial district and back to work

indicators.note: the travel piece goes round the others

parts.note: to go is to travel
EC is the postcode of the City of London, its financial centre

indicators.note: the back, or final letter, of the word work

explanation.surface: Someone travels round the City and then goes back to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A gecko is a small climbing lizard, a reptile.

clue.text: Freight, having origin in Colchis, on relevant ship?

indicators.note: the first letter of Colchis is taken

parts.note: the Argo carried Jason to Colchis for the Golden Fleece, so it is the ship relevant here

explanation.surface: Freight from Colchis travels aboard the appropriate vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is goods carried by ship, freight.

clue.text: See 10
Boy returned with Jewish girl — husband out for drink

indicators.note: the boy's name is sent back, read right to left

parts.note: Ron is a boy's name

indicators.note: the husband is left out of the girl's name

parts.note: Esther is a Jewish girl's name, from the biblical queen

explanation.surface: A boy comes back with his Jewish girlfriend, her husband having gone out drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns RON to NOR; 'out' takes H from ESTHER to leave ESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A nor'wester is a stiff glass of strong liquor, a dram.

clue.text: Posh knight, loaded, not exactly bright

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh
N is the chess notation for knight
loaded and lit both mean drunk

explanation.surface: A posh knight who is drunk is not the sharpest.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlit means without lights on, dark, which is hardly bright.

clue.text: Maiden gone, bloke on my back gives fictitious name

indicators.note: the maiden is removed from the bloke

parts.note: a man is a bloke
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: the word my is read backwards

explanation.surface: A maiden has left, and a man on my back gives a false name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' takes M from MAN to leave AN; 'back' turns MY to YM.
explanation.definitionFit: An anonym is an assumed name, a pseudonym.

clue.text: Tube or Metro in motion?

parts.note: London's Tube and the Paris Metro are both underground railways, ways beneath the streets, and a moving train is in progress

explanation.definitionFit: Something under way is in progress, moving; the clue also reads it as a subterranean route.
